title: Minimum Number of Days to Make m Bouquets
prompt: Given an integer array `bloomDay`, an integer `m`, and an integer `k`, return the minimum number of days needed to make `m` bouquets from the garden, or `-1` if it is impossible. The garden consists of `n` flowers; the i-th flower will bloom on day `bloomDay[i]`. To make a bouquet you need `k` adjacent flowers from the garden that have all already bloomed, and a flower can only belong to one bouquet.

examples.explanation: After day 3, the blooms are [x,_,x,_,x]. Picking any three of them makes 3 bouquets of 1 flower each.
There aren't enough adjacent flowers to make 3 bouquets of 2 flowers each, no matter how many days pass.

hints: If m * k is more than the total number of flowers, it's immediately impossible regardless of how many days pass.
For a fixed number of days, you know exactly which flowers have bloomed, and can greedily scan for runs of k or more consecutive bloomed flowers to count how many bouquets can be made.

The number of bouquets makeable is monotonically non-decreasing as days increase, so binary search on the day count over the range [min(bloomDay), max(bloomDay)] for the earliest day where m bouquets are achievable.

solution.approach: First rule out impossibility: if m * k exceeds the total flower count, no amount of waiting helps. Otherwise binary search over the possible day values, from the earliest to the latest bloom day. For a candidate day, scan the garden and greedily count consecutive runs of already-bloomed flowers, converting each run of length L into L // k bouquets; summing these gives the total bouquets makeable by that day. This total is monotonically non-decreasing in the day count, so binary search for the earliest day where the total reaches m, giving an O(n log(max(bloomDay))) solution.
